notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware run. The upstream class inherits ManiSkill BaseEnv and imports sapien, torch and mani_skill (pyproject.toml:10, :26-32), which are not importable where the gate ran, so the fake backend is the package's own pure Python kinematic stand-in and was never compared with the upstream environment; the unlisted sim backend (gymnasium.make of BunchOfColors3-v0) was not run. NOT COVERED: the ManiSkill state observation array, whose exact size depends on the robot and sensors and is not stated in the clone; the fake returns a seven-value proprio-like stand-in in the documented layout and the fidelity gaps say so. Also not covered: rigid-body/contact dynamics, the Panda robot, the nine-cube scene, the camera sensors, the task success condition and the upstream reward (the fake returns reward 0 and only truncates at the registered 120-step limit). timestep_ms is 0 because the clone states no physics or control timestep (SimConfig at bunch_of_colors.py:53-59). Expected warnings of this Gymnasium family driver: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (it only sets the seed of the next reset), G7.MAYBE_ABSENT for action_space, observation_space and reset (inherited from ManiSkill BaseEnv, outside the clone), and four G8.NO_UNIT for the integer inputs the bridge derives (seed twice, ticks, action.values[*]). No G4 warnings; the action bound is the documented normalized pd_ee_delta_pose space (docs/source/observation_space.rst:147-172) and is derived by the bridge from the environment, not declared as a driver Limit. Only catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue requests. gate.digest is the digest the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
